```sh
kafka topic delete <topics...>
```

Delete one or more topics

## Arguments

| Argument    | Description           |
| ----------- | --------------------- |
| `topics...` | topic names to delete |

Shared options and defaults: [connection profiles, JSON output, logging and help](../../../global-options/).

## Defaults

Confirmation is required unless --yes or configured confirmation policy permits it. --force overrides internal-topic and batch-size protections.

## Before you run

Deletes topics and their records. There is no preview flag or undelete operation. Confirm the cluster and backups before bypassing confirmation with --yes or protections with --force.

## Flags

| Flag                 | Description                                              |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--brokers <string>` | comma-separated broker list, e.g. localhost:9092         |
| `--if-exists`        | treat a missing topic as success                         |
| `--yes`              | confirm the deletion without an interactive prompt       |
| `--force`            | override the internal-topic and batch-size safety checks |

## Examples

```sh
kafka topic delete orders --brokers localhost:9092 --yes
kafka topic delete __consumer_offsets --brokers localhost:9092 --yes --force
```

## Output

Illustrative, abbreviated output. Empty arrays show the result envelope; actual entries, identifiers, optional fields and broker errors depend on the request and cluster.

With `--json`:

```json
{
  "results": [
    {
      "topic": "events",
      "ok": true
    }
  ]
}
```

Declared exit codes: `0`, `1`, `2`, `4`, `5`. See the exit-code reference for meanings.
